text.text_excerpt: La Divina recently opened its third location on the campus of Loyola University and unlike most campus iterations of local restaurants, it tastes just like their real-world locations around the city. The location is on the bottom floor of Carrollton Hall, a campus residence building and is accessible to the public with no problem. Park on Calhoun and walk into campus on Lasalle Place. I've had two paninis so far and enjoyed them. The bread is particularly good. See note below. Like at their other locations, they use as many local and seasonal ingredients as possible. The gelato is made with some seasonal fruit too. I had a good laugh at the booze flavored gelato (rum? bourbon? I forget......

When La Divina opened their third location right on Loyola campus I was sooo excited! The panini's are made fresh and to order! My favorite is the taccino with comes with avocado! The gelato is soo goo too! and my favorite dessert are the apricot oat bars! This place is just amazing fr a coffee break and a nice lunch on campus. there is always good music so it is also a nice place to study.

La Divina is perfect for late-night cravings that don't involve you having to stand next to drunken students while loud music plays in the background. Instead, you're more likely to chat up a conversation with a bunch of music students who don't have enough time to go get drunk. Being located on Loyola's main campus makes it a great alternative to boring college cafeteria food made of who-knows-what. And all the food ingredients are locally grown and harvested, so don't worry about having to pay Sodexo for anything
